module_name: LLMs as Annotators and Coders: Reliability, Bias, Human-in-the-Loop
module_description: Module 13 addresses the newest standard practice: using LLMs to label/code large corpora (sentiment, frames, relevance, stance, ideology, topic labels). It teaches prompt/codebook design, multiple sampling and aggregation, validation against human gold sets, reliability gates (Cohen's kappa), bias and stereotype risks, cost/latency trade-offs, and when to distill to a smaller classifier. Includes the human-in-the-loop pattern now required for publication-grade work.
core_concepts: Zero-shot vs few-shot vs fine-tuned coding
Bias, stereotype amplification, and logit/prompt sensitivity
Distillation to cheap classifiers for scale
learning_outcomes: C3 Design a prompt-based codebook for a coding task
C4 Validate LLM labels against a human gold set and report kappa
C5 Identify bias risks and mitigate with sampling and review
methods_models: Prompt engineering, structured output (JSON), self-consistency, batch APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic batch, VLLM/local), kappa agreement
Distillation training (student model on LLM labels)
evaluation_metrics: Cohen's kappa vs human coders, Krippendorff's alpha for multi-coder, F1 vs gold, consistency across prompt variants, cost per 1k items
pitfalls_limitations: False confidence from high accuracy on easy items, bias on identity categories, prompt sensitivity, silent drift with model version updates, leakage of sensitive data into APIs
tools_stack: LLM SDKs (OpenAI/Anthropic/open-source), DSPy-style optimization, Google Sheets/Excel for gold sets, kappa libraries
commercial_platforms: Not applicable; this is a methods module that replaces manual annotation
tools_access_cost: API pricing per token; local open models free but require hardware; reliability work requires human coder time
lab_activities: Run a small coding task with LLM, human-code a 200-item gold set, report kappa, iterate prompts, then distill
datasets_apis: Gold set from an Indonesian social corpus (e.g. stance on an issue)
assessment_methods: Lab notebook submission plus a 1-page interpretation with error analysis; graded on correctness, interpretation and documentation
data_collection_workflow: Collect posts -> clean text -> build annotation/codebook (human + LLM) -> validate with kappa -> train/evaluate -> archive labelled data and prompts
textbooks: Tornberg, 'Best practices for text annotation with LLMs' (2024)
Gilardi et al., 'LLMs outperform expert coders' (2024)
Bermejo et al. (2025) LLMs vs outsourced crowd coders
key_papers: Schroeder et al. (2025) human-in-the-loop for subjective coding tasks
Carlson (2025) LLM annotation in management research
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: LLM annotation went from novelty to expected practice with mandatory validation and bias checks; batch APIs and prompt optimization (DSPy) made it scalable
industry_relevance: Core competency for social-listening analyst, insights researcher and content-strategy roles; employers (Pulsar, Talkwalker, Meltwater, Brandwatch) list sentiment/topic extraction as the default screening task for junior analysts.
localization_context: Indonesia-specific models and lexicons (IndoBERT family, NusaBERT, InSet) plus local datasets (Indonesian sentiment/emotion/hoax sets) are used as the primary lab material, because English-oriented models underperform on code-mixed colloquial Indonesian.
ethics_regulation: Annotation labor and consent, model reporting of error rates, and disclosure that automated affective labels on individuals can misrepresent them; UU PDP applies when the corpus contains identifiable user text.
case_study_scenarios: Code 10,000 Indonesian posts for stance on a policy issue using LLM + human validation and report reliability.
deliverable_format: Codebook + gold set + kappa report + distilled classifier
